You check whether a knowledge-base article answers a support ticket for a clinical practice-management product. Set answers_ticket to true only if following the article would resolve what the ticket actually asks. An article about a related task does not answer it: an article on placing an order does not answer a question about cancelling one. If the ticket asks for more than one thing, the article must answer all of them: an article that covers only part of the request does not answer it. Give the reason in one sentence.

Reply with only a JSON object and no other text.
Output: grounding.
The JSON object must match this JSON schema:
{"additionalProperties": false, "description": "Whether the best-matching article actually answers the ticket.", "properties": {"answers_ticket": {"title": "Answers Ticket", "type": "boolean"}, "reason": {"minLength": 1, "title": "Reason", "type": "string"}}, "required": ["answers_ticket", "reason"], "title": "grounding", "type": "object"}

Article id: customize-notification-templates
Article: Customize patient notification and message templates
Practice managers can tailor automated patient alerts to match clinic branding. Only administrators and designated managers have permission to edit these settings.

1. Navigate to **Settings > Communications > Templates**.
2. Select the category tab, such as **Appointment Confirmations** or **Billing Notices**.
3. Choose the template you wish to modify and click **Edit**.
4. Draft your message using available placeholder tags from the sidebar (e.g., `{{patient_first_name}}`, `{{appointment_date}}`).
5. Click **Preview** to review the rendered text, then select **Save Changes**.

### Limits and Conditions
* Templates cannot exceed 480 characters to comply with standard SMS gateway limits.
* Custom HTML styling is supported only in email templates.

### Troubleshooting
If placeholder tags fail to populate when sent, verify that the tag syntax matches the exact spelling in the sidebar glossary. Unmatched brackets (like missing the closing `}}`) will trigger a syntax validation error and prevent saving. If emails fail to deliver after updating, check that your sender domain authentication remains active under **Settings > Communications > Domain Setup**.

Ticket:
Confused about notification template syntax and formatting

I am completely turned around trying to fix our automated appointment reminders and billing notice texts. I went into the messaging setup area and tried tweaking the template text, but now the syntax tags look completely broken and I keep getting error messages when I try to save. Also, I am not sure how the variables map anymore. Could someone please walk me through how to format these templates properly?
